ANSWER: The function that decides whether text looks like a secret is **`secret_kind`** in `src/memory/guard.rs` (line 53). It first checks the text against a set of named regex patterns (private keys, AWS keys, GitHub tokens, JWTs, etc.). If none match, it uses `LONG_TOKEN` (a regex for any 32+ character alphanumeric run) to find candidate tokens, and passes each to the helper **`looks_random`** (line 62 in the same file) to distinguish random-looking base64 keys from structured identifiers like hex hashes or base32 IDs. `looks_random` does so by requiring the token to contain mixed case and digits, then computing Shannon entropy — tokens with entropy above 4.2 bits per character are flagged as `"high-entropy token"`. Both functions are in `src/memory/guard.rs`.

CONFIDENCE: high
